# Testament of Benjamin — 12
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

**1** The copy of the words of Benjamin, which he commanded his sons after he had lived a hundred and twenty-five years. **2** And he kissed them, and said: As Isaac was born to Abraham in his old age, so also was I to Jacob. **3** And since Rachel my mother died in giving me birth, I had no milk; therefore I was suckled by Bilhah her handmaid. **4** For Rachel remained barren for twelve years after she had borne Joseph; and she prayed the Lord with fasting twelve years, and she conceived and bare me. **5** For our father loved Rachel dearly, and prayed that he might see two sons born of her.

**2** And when I went into Egypt, to Joseph, and my brother recognised me, he said unto me: What did they tell my father when they sold me? **2** And I said to him: They dabbled thy coat with blood and sent it to him, and said, Know whether this be thy son's coat. **3** And he said unto me: Even so, brother, when they stripped me of my garment they gave me to eat, and said, Weep not, Joseph, for we will sell thee for gold, and thy God will be with thee. **4** And one of them repented greatly that he had sold Joseph; for he feared greatly the face of God. **5** And when Joseph saw that the spirit of Reuben was thus, he had compassion on him.

**3** After this, my children, love ye the Lord God of heaven and earth, and keep his commandments, following the example of the good and holy man Joseph. **2** And let your mind be unto good, even as ye know me; for he that hath his mind right seeth all things rightly. **3** Fear ye the Lord, and love your neighbour; and even though the spirits of Beliar claim you to afflict you with every evil, yet shall they not have dominion over you, even as they had not over Joseph my brother. **4** How many men wished to slay him, and God shielded him! **5** For he that feareth God and loveth his neighbour cannot be smitten by the spirit of Beliar, being shielded by the fear of God. **6** Nor can he be ruled over by the device of men or of beasts, for he is helped by the Lord through the love which he hath towards his neighbour.

**4** For Joseph also besought our father to pray for his brethren, that the Lord would not impute to them as sin whatever evil they had done unto him. **2** And thus Jacob cried out: My good child, thou hast prevailed over the bowels of thy father Jacob. **3** And he embraced him and kissed him for two hours, saying: In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven concerning the Lamb of God, and Saviour of the world, and that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless one shall die for ungodly men in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and of Israel, and shall destroy Beliar and his servants. **4** See ye, therefore, my children, the end of the good man? **5** Be followers of his compassion therefore with a good mind, that ye also may wear crowns of glory.

**5** For the good man hath not a dark eye; for he showeth mercy to all men, sinners though they be, even though they devise evil concerning him. **2** So he that doeth good overcometh the evil, being shielded by the good; and the beloved of God is loved of every man. **3** Flee ye therefore the malice of Beliar; for he giveth a sword to them that obey him. **4** And the sword is the mother of seven evils: first, it is obtained through Beliar in bloodshed; the second is ruin; the third is tribulation; the fourth is exile; the fifth is dearth; the sixth is panic; the seventh is desolation.

**6** Therefore was Cain given over to seven vengeances by God, for in every hundred years the Lord brought one plague upon him. **2** And when he was two hundred years old he began to suffer, and in the nine hundredth year he was destroyed. **3** For on account of Abel his brother he was judged, but on account of his own wickedness he was destroyed.

**7** And now, my children, do the truth each one to his neighbour, and keep the law of the Lord and his commandments. **2** For these things do I leave you instead of all inheritance. **3** Do ye also give them to your children for an everlasting possession; for so did both Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob. **4** For all these things they gave us for an inheritance, saying: Keep the commandments of God, until the Lord shall reveal his salvation to all Gentiles. **5** And then shall ye see Enoch, Noah, and Shem, and Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, rising on the right hand in gladness. **6** Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven, who appeared upon earth in the form of a man of humility. **7** And as many as believe on him on the earth shall rejoice with him. **8** Then also shall all men rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. **9** And the Lord shall judge Israel first, for their unrighteousness; for when he appeared as God in the flesh to deliver them they believed him not.

**8** And then shall he judge all the Gentiles, as many as believed him not when he appeared upon earth. **2** And he shall convict Israel through the chosen ones of the Gentiles, even as he reproved Esau through the Midianites, who deceived their brethren, so that they fell into fornication, and idolatry; and they were alienated from God, becoming therefore children in the portion of them that fear the Lord. **3** If ye therefore, my children, walk in holiness according to the commandments of the Lord, ye shall again dwell securely with me, and all Israel shall be gathered unto the Lord.

**9** And I shall no longer be called a ravening wolf on account of your ravages, but a worker of the Lord distributing food to them that work what is good. **2** And there shall arise in the latter days one beloved of the Lord, of the tribe of Judah and of Levi, a doer of his good pleasure in his mouth, with new knowledge enlightening the Gentiles. **3** Until the consummation of the age shall he be in the synagogues of the Gentiles, and among their rulers, as a strain of music in the mouth of all. **4** And he shall be inscribed in the holy books, both his work and his word, and he shall be a chosen one of God for ever.

**10** And now, my children, obey the Lord, and flee from the evil deeds of Beliar. **2** And when he had said these things Benjamin fell into a sweet sleep. **3** And rising in the morning they found that he had died. **4** And after thirty days his sons carried him into Hebron and buried him with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Benjamin*
